requirement:
Documented annotations are browsable regardless of their last recorded
review result. The book neither filters them by acceptance nor checks whether
they are used to satisfy current measured coverage. Source items and locations
remain connected to the current source notes under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.current`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps.accepted` has no implementation roots, and none are needed. The text has no MUST, SHOULD or MAY clause. It describes observable book behavior in three statements:

- "Documented annotations are browsable regardless of their last recorded review result."
- "The book neither filters them by acceptance nor checks whether they are used to satisfy current measured coverage."
- "Source items and locations remain connected to the current source notes."

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. Any rendering pipeline that shows every documented annotation, applies no acceptance filter and links items to the current notes meets all three statements. The pipeline could be built many ways, so the construction is discretionary. The last statement defers to `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.current`. That requirement is cited as context only and is judged separately. The requirement has no outgoing Implements edges, which is consistent with having no structural obligation to evidence.

behavioral: The tests cover each obligation of `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps.accepted`.

**Browsable regardless of the last recorded review result.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[overview_shows_missing_unreadable_and_recorded_reviews_with_current_justifications]` renders the annotated item under six review states: missing, true, false, FIXME, invalid JSON and unreadable. Each time it asserts that the item is still listed, that its justification is shown, and that the matching recorded-review label appears. It also asserts that no acceptance wording and no staleness wording appears. `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_browses_all_proposals_while_cli_checks_reviews_and_measurements]` repeats the missing, true, false and FIXME states through `book::populate_in`. It asserts that `fn[b]` is listed in every state and stays in the data-file `code.rs` map.

**No filtering by acceptance.** The same `check.rs` test shows `fn[b]` while the CLI report fails because the review is missing. It shows `fn[b]` again after the review is recorded true.

**No check on whether the annotation is used to satisfy measured coverage.** In `check.rs`, `fn[b]` is listed and the recorded-true label is shown both when the CLI report passes and after the profile file is deleted so that it fails. The assertion that the second render equals the first shows the book output does not change with the measured-coverage outcome. `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_ignores_saved_measurements_and_preserves_artifacts]` shows the rendered chapters are identical whether or not saved measurement attempts exist, even when the attempt metadata is invalid or empty. It also shows that no `target` directory is created and no saved test names leak into the output.

**Items and locations stay connected to current source notes** (context from the cited `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.current`). The `book.rs` overview test changes the source text and checks that the justification updates: the updated explanation replaces the original, and the no-tracked-justification message appears when the doc comment is removed. The review file bytes stay unchanged. The `check.rs` test checks the item's source location and data-file link, and checks that the justification changes after the source is edited.

I found no behavioural obligation without a test, and every relevant test carries a {test} reference to the subject.
